problem: Compare three fictional vendor proposals for an IT service. Procurement staff need a clear comparison of total price, delivery time, warranty, and compliance with mandatory requirements, followed by a justified recommendation. Build a working demo with GLM 4.7 Flash as the runtime model.
current_process: A buyer manually reads three vendor proposals for each quotation, copies their terms into a spreadsheet, checks mandatory requirements and decides which proposal offers the best fit.
users: Internal procurement analysts and IT managers using fictional demo data.
successful_interaction: The buyer enters a quotation ID, sees all three vendors in a comparison table, key risks or missing requirements, and a recommended vendor with reasoning grounded in the saved proposals. They can inspect RFQ001, RFQ002 and RFQ003, with different winners in each case.
workflow: 1. User enters a quotation ID and requests a standard comparison. 2. Load the quotation requirements and all three vendor proposals from its JSON sample in S3. 3. Compare total price in BRL, delivery days, warranty months and mandatory requirements. Exclude proposals that fail mandatory requirements from the recommendation and explain why. 4. Show the three proposals side by side, risks, recommended vendor and justification. 5. The human makes the final purchasing decision outside the app. No purchasing or messaging tools.
human_in_loop: The recommendation is advisory. A human makes the final decision. Do not execute purchases, send messages or contact suppliers.
frequency: On demand for a small technical demo, fewer than 20 comparisons per day.
data_inputs: Only fictional JSON stored in S3. Generate three quotation examples RFQ001, RFQ002, RFQ003, each with a quotation ID, service description, mandatory requirements and exactly three vendor proposals containing vendor ID/name, total_price_brl, delivery_days, warranty_months, meets_requirements and notes. Use a different best vendor for each quotation. Store each quotation at <quotation_id>/profile.json so it matches the shared profile retriever; use the same IDs in the UI examples. No PDFs, attachments, web browsing or external databases.
data_outputs: A web screen with a comparison table (three vendor rows, price, delivery, warranty, requirement compliance), attention points, recommended vendor and a concise justification citing actual proposal values. A structured JSON response should provide the same fields for the screen. Display all three test quotation IDs as quick-fill examples.
compliance: Use synthetic data only. No personal data. Do not invent proposal values or silently fabricate missing quotations. Use zai.glm-4.7-flash for runtime inference. Return an understandable error if a quotation cannot be found. No external actions.
existing_systems: Only the existing AWS demo infrastructure: S3 for sample JSON, Bedrock GLM 4.7 Flash, AgentCore runtime and the generated web UI. No external APIs, document extraction, email, purchasing integrations or web search.
